learn.title: Choose the family from the data
learn.body: Look at how the output changes when the input goes up by 1. A constant difference points to a linear model. A constant ratio points to an exponential model. A constant second difference points to a quadratic.

learn.title: Use and question the model
learn.body: Squares $1,4,9,16$ have differences $3,5,7$ and second differences $2,2$, so they are quadratic. A model only works inside the range of its data. A tank cannot hold negative water, so always ask what the numbers mean.

questions.explanation: The differences are all 3, which means linear.
The ratios are all 2, so each step doubles.

questions.prompt: A pool has 12 cm of water and gains 3 cm per hour. How many cm after 5 hours?
A tank holds 200 L and loses 10 percent each hour, $V=200(0.9)^t$. How many liters after 2 hours?
A constant \_\_ between outputs suggests an exponential model.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the same factor each step is exponential.

questions.prompt: The values $1,4,9,16$ have second differences of:
questions.explanation: First differences are $3,5,7$, and those differ by $2,2$. So it is quadratic.

questions.prompt: Match the pattern to the model.
questions.explanation: Each family has its own signature in the data.

questions.prompt: A model fitted to ages 10 to 20 predicts for age 90. What should you do?
choices: Be cautious, it is far outside the data
questions.explanation: Predictions far outside the fitted range are unreliable.

questions.prompt: Build a model from a table. Put the steps in order.
steps: Find the constants from the data
questions.explanation: Look at the pattern first, then fit and check.
